headword: {終身雇用|しゅうしんこよう}

definitions.explanation: A Japanese employment practice in which companies hire employees straight out of school and retain them until retirement. One of the three pillars of traditional Japanese corporate culture, along with seniority-based pay and enterprise unions.

examples.japanese: {終身雇用|しゅうしんこよう}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{崩|くず}れ→崩れる：04248_kuzureru⟧つつ⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: The lifetime employment system is crumbling.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{終身雇用|しゅうしんこよう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}→当たり前：01685_atarimae⟧だった。
examples.english: In my father's era, lifetime employment was taken for granted.

examples.japanese: {終身雇用|しゅうしんこよう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{前提|ぜんてい}→前提：08240_zentei⟧とした⟦{人事|じんじ}→人事：00126_jinji⟧⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{見直|みなお}し→見直し：09340_minaoshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}んでいる→進む：01225_susumu⟧。
examples.english: Personnel systems based on the assumption of lifetime employment are being reviewed.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Lifetime employment ({終身雇用|しゅうしんこよう}) was a defining feature of Japan's postwar corporate culture, particularly at large companies. Together with ⟦{年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ}→年功序列：12532_nenkoujoretsu⟧ (seniority-based pay) and {企業別組合|きぎょうべつくみあい} (enterprise unions), it formed the "three sacred treasures" of Japanese management. Since the 1990s recession, this practice has been gradually declining as companies shift toward more flexible employment.
